newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks absorb profit-taking to end up.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks absorb profit-taking to end up.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks snared another 1996 closing high on Wednesday, despite some profit-taking after recent gains, as investors remained bullish on the outlook of the market.
"The overall market tone remains quite firm," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
"We saw some profit-taking in the morning but it seemed to be very well absorbed and buying interest drove up the index."
The Hang Seng index closed 30.66 points higher at 11,951.88, the highest close since February 4, 1994. The blue chip index hit a 1996 intra-day high at 11,956.16 during the session.
Turnover was a busy HK$6.26 billion compared to Tuesday's HK6.06 billion.
"It's a fairly healthy consolidation," said Miles Remington, sales trader at Crosby Securities.
He said some investors had been sidelined ahead of Governor Chris Patten's annual policy speech. "There was a little bit of holding back waiting for the removal of any potential bad news."
But traders said they did not expect the speech to have an impact on share prices.
"I think people are paying more attention to Sun Hung Kai Properties' results," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
Sun Hung Kai Properties was due to release its final results after the market close on Wednesday. The stock ended the session down HK$0.75 at HK$81.75.
"Sun Hung Kai was being sold down aggressively on the belief that its growth will be below 10 percent," said Remington.
Other property shares came under some pressure with Henderson Land ending down HK$0.25 at HK$66.00 and Hysan Development shedding HK$0.25 to HK$24.10.
Sino Land rose HK$0.15 to HK$8.60. It reported a 60 percent drop in 1995/96 net profit to HK$1.15 billion which was expected by the market.
Mak said the underlying tone in the market remained "fairly strong" and he expected more gains ahead.

"There might be some follow-through buying tomorrow," he said, adding however that the Hang Seng index may not reach 12,000 points this week with some investors possibly hesitating ahead of the release of U.S. employment data on Friday.
"Overall I think local shares need some sort of consolidation first ahead of 12,000 resistance," said Kwong.
"I'm still skeptical about whether there is sufficient momentum to breach that level," he added.
